spec.task_context: Shadow Work has 5 policy domains with 14 total stances. The player's worldview is emergent from card choices across 353 issue YAML files spanning 2025 near-term crises through 2525 post-human existential scenarios. Axes must be recognizable to players from diverse political traditions.

frontmatter.description: Whether proposed ideological axes produce mechanically different gameplay outcomes when mapped to the 14 policy stances across 5 domains
frontmatter.name: fd-axis-mechanical-distinctness

anti_overlap: fd-axis-temporal-validity covers whether axes remain legible across the 2025-to-2525 scenario span
fd-axis-orthogonality covers whether proposed axes are statistically independent from each other
fd-axis-ideological-authenticity covers whether axes map to real-world political positions players recognize
spec.decision_lens: Prioritizes findings where two opposite axis poles select the same stance in any domain — that is a mechanical null axis. Secondarily flags axes where the stance mapping is valid but the base_cost() difference is small enough (<20 units) that players cannot feel the distinction.
spec.focus: Whether proposed ideological axes produce mechanically different gameplay outcomes when mapped to the 14 policy stances across 5 domains
spec.name: fd-axis-mechanical-distinctness
spec.persona: A game systems designer who has built political simulation games and knows the failure mode where 'distinct' ideology labels all route to the same deployment choice. This agent traces each axis value to its downstream stance selection, auto-deploy behavior, and cost function to find where axes collapse into each other.
review_areas: For each proposed axis, enumerate which of the 14 PolicyStance values it would prefer or suppress — if two axis poles converge on the same stance set for any domain, the axis has no mechanical purchase in that domain

Test the Energy domain specifically: Stabilize/Liberalize/Nationalize/Extract span a wide range — verify any proposed axis can differentiate at least 3 of these 4 stances, since Energy has the most stances and should be the sharpest discriminator

Verify that Labor domain stances (Protect/Deregulate/Mediate) are each exclusively preferred by at least one axis position — if no axis separates Protect from Mediate, those stances cannot be reached by principled play

Check whether the Technology domain's Regulate/Deregulate/Monitor triad is fully covered — Deregulate is shared with Labor, so confirm the axis encoding handles cross-domain stance reuse without conflating unrelated issue types

Examine the base_cost() spread across the stances an axis would select: Aggressive (180) vs Diplomatic (70) is a meaningful cost signal; an axis that only differentiates Monitor (40) vs Monitor (40) is a no-op

For each axis, identify at least one issue YAML from data/issues/ whose parameters directly map to a stance preference — if no issue can be linked to an axis value, the axis is unmeasurable from card history
success_hints: Each axis pole should deterministically select a different primary stance in at least 3 of 5 domains — if an axis only differentiates in 1 domain it is a domain-specific slider, not a worldview axis

A player pattern of Nationalize+Protect+Reform+Regulate+Defensive should classify unambiguously to one axis extreme; Liberalize+Deregulate+Leverage+Monitor+Diplomatic to the other — no axis should be ambiguous about these canonical patterns
spec.task_context: Shadow Work has 5 policy domains (Energy, Labor, Governance, Technology, Security) with 14 total stances encoded in PolicyStance enum. The player's worldview is emergent from card choices — axes must be inferrable from accumulated stance history, not declared.

frontmatter.description: Whether proposed axes are genuinely independent dimensions or correlated proxies for the same underlying ideological signal
frontmatter.name: fd-axis-orthogonality

anti_overlap: fd-axis-mechanical-distinctness covers whether individual axes produce different stance selections
fd-axis-variety-coverage covers whether the axis system produces enough combinatorial variety
fd-axis-temporal-validity covers whether axes remain valid over time
spec.decision_lens: Prioritizes axis pairs where the Pearson correlation of their stance preference vectors exceeds 0.6 — such pairs add little information beyond the first axis. Secondarily flags axes that are theoretically independent but empirically collapse in the issue space.
spec.focus: Whether proposed axes are genuinely independent dimensions or correlated proxies for the same underlying ideological signal
spec.name: fd-axis-orthogonality
spec.persona: A political scientist and data analyst who has applied principal component analysis to voting records and knows that most political behavior is explained by 1-2 independent factors despite having hundreds of apparent dimensions.
review_areas: For each pair of proposed axes, construct their implied stance preference vectors across all 14 PolicyStance values and compute the dot product — a high dot product indicates the axes reward the same stances and are not independent

Check whether economic-left/right and state-capacity axes are being proposed separately when they are known to be empirically correlated — verify they diverge on at least Technology and Security domains

Test the nationalist axis against the security axis: Aggressive Security correlates with nationalist positions — verify a nationalist-internationalist axis and a hawk-dove axis are separable by identifying issues where they predict opposite stances
Examine whether a techno-optimist/techno-pessimist axis and an authoritarian/libertarian axis are being conflated: surveillance technology and Regulate/Monitor stances appeal to both
For each proposed axis, identify 3 issues from data/issues/ where it predicts the opposite stance from all other proposed axes — if no such issues exist, the axis is not adding independent signal

Check whether any axis is a domain-specific restatement of another: an 'energy sovereignty' axis might be orthogonal to a 'market vs state' axis in theory but collapse because Nationalize and Extract are both chosen by sovereigntists AND statists
success_hints: For a set of N proposed axes, the product of their separations should produce at least 2^N distinct ideological regions — if 5 axes only produce 8 distinguishable combinations instead of 32, at least 2 axes are redundant
There should exist at least 5 issues in data/issues/ for each proposed axis where that axis is the primary predictor of stance choice and the other axes are neutral or conflicting
spec.task_context: Shadow Work uses an AgentIdeology struct with economic, social, and nationalist axes plus conviction. The task is to evaluate whether proposed additional or replacement axes are genuinely orthogonal to these existing dimensions and to each other.

frontmatter.description: Whether proposed axes remain meaningful and non-degenerate across the 500-year scenario span from 2025 near-term issues through 2525 post-human existential scenarios
frontmatter.name: fd-axis-temporal-validity

anti_overlap: fd-axis-mechanical-distinctness covers whether axes differentiate the current 14-stance set
fd-axis-ideological-authenticity covers whether axes map to real-world recognized positions
fd-axis-orthogonality covers whether axes are independent of each other
spec.decision_lens: Prioritizes axes whose poles become synonymous or meaningless in future scenarios — an axis that perfectly differentiates 2025 energy policy but collapses to a single pole when energy is post-scarcity is a temporal validity failure.
spec.focus: Whether proposed axes remain meaningful and non-degenerate across the 500-year scenario span from 2025 near-term issues through 2525 post-human existential scenarios
spec.name: fd-axis-temporal-validity
spec.persona: A futures studies researcher and game designer who has built long-span historical games (Europa Universalis, Civilization) and thinks carefully about how political categories dissolve and reconstitute over time.
review_areas: For each proposed axis, identify the earliest scenario where the axis would stop producing different gameplay outcomes — scan the issue corpus for temporal markers and test whether the axis still differentiates stance choices

Check the Security domain specifically: Defensive/Aggressive/Diplomatic map cleanly to 2025 geopolitics, but do these stances remain distinct when security threats are synthetic biology releases, AI-driven cyberwar, or consciousness-merging?

Test whether the Labor domain stances (Protect/Deregulate/Mediate) retain meaning when artificial-wombs-and-gestation-outsourcing and automated-companion-replacements dominate — 'labor' as a category may dissolve
Verify that the Governance domain stances (Reform/Infiltrate/Leverage) scale to scenarios with algorithmic-governance-proliferation and consciousness-merger-phenomenon

Examine whether any axis is purely reactive to 21st-century scarcity assumptions: if Technology axis differentiates based on access to computing resources, does it collapse in a post-scarcity compute world?

Check whether the axes can absorb entirely new issue categories not yet represented in the corpus — if a 2400 scenario introduces mind-uploading as a policy domain, does the axis system still classify the player's position?
success_hints: For at least 3 representative issues from each century bracket, the axis should produce a non-degenerate classification

The axis labels should be abstract enough that they describe durable tensions rather than specific policy debates — 'state capacity vs market autonomy' survives longer than 'fossil fuel subsidy vs carbon tax'
spec.task_context: Shadow Work's 353 issue YAML files span from 2025 near-term crises through far-future post-human scenarios. The axis system must classify player behavior coherently across this full span.

frontmatter.description: Whether the axis system produces sufficient combinatorial variety so that no two meaningfully different player patterns map to the same axis position
frontmatter.name: fd-axis-variety-coverage

anti_overlap: fd-axis-mechanical-distinctness covers whether individual axes differentiate the stance set
fd-axis-orthogonality covers whether axes are statistically independent
fd-axis-ideological-authenticity covers whether axis positions correspond to real-world traditions
spec.decision_lens: Prioritizes axis configurations that create large 'dead zones' — regions of the stance-combination space that no axis position covers uniquely — and axes that are so coarse that many distinct political philosophies hash to the same classification.
spec.focus: Whether the axis system produces sufficient combinatorial variety so that no two meaningfully different player patterns map to the same axis position
spec.name: fd-axis-variety-coverage
spec.persona: A combinatorics-minded game designer who has worked on classification and tagging systems and knows the failure mode of under-parameterized taxonomy.
review_areas: Enumerate the practical stance combination space: 4 Energy stances x 3 Labor x 3 Governance x 3 Technology x 3 Security = 324 unique full-domain patterns — map a sample of 20 politically-coherent patterns onto the proposed axes and count how many map to distinct axis positions

Test for the 'centrist collapse' problem: players who choose Stabilize/Mediate/Leverage/Monitor/Diplomatic are genuinely centrist, but other moderate combinations might also hash to center — verify center-of-axes is not a catch-all

Check whether single-domain deviance is detectable: a player who is Aggressive only in Security while being Diplomatic everywhere else should classify differently from a consistently Diplomatic player

Evaluate the minimum number of card choices required before the axis system can assign a non-degenerate classification — if 20+ cards are needed, the player will be unclassified for most of early-game
Verify that partial patterns (player has set stances in only 2 of 5 domains) produce a sensible partial classification rather than defaulting to neutral
success_hints: For a set of N proposed axes, the product of their separations should produce at least 2^N distinct ideological regions
A player who has made 10 card choices spanning at least 3 domains should have a provisional axis classification with >70% confidence
spec.task_context: Shadow Work has 5 policy domains with 14 stances producing 324 full-domain combinations. The player's worldview is emergent from card choices — the axis system must assign a legible worldview position from partial, noisy stance histories.

anti_overlap: fd-emergent-narrative-design-legibility covers player-facing story legibility and gameplay interestingness — this agent covers only bench-instrument validity: reproducibility, discriminative power between policies, and referee-harness integrity.

fd-simulation-calibration-validity-methodology covers general ABM/CSS calibration methodology (identifiability, sample size, reference-class grounding) — this agent covers only the ShadowBench-specific consequences of calibration choices (policy discriminability, byte-identical referee determinism, actor-class attribution needs), not general calibration soundness.
spec.decision_lens: Prioritizes findings where a calibration or trigger-condition choice that looks correct from a game-design or general-calibration lens actually damages ShadowBench's specific requirements: reproducible byte-identical reference streams for the referee harness, sufficient baseline-outcome variance for policies to be discriminable against, and freedom from the anti-gaming concerns already flagged in samsara-trigger-conditions.md (§3 Candidate B's 'tuning_dials(run) = defaults' clause). Deprioritizes pure narrative/legibility findings that don't bear on measurement validity for cross-policy comparison.
spec.focus: Whether the calibration choice (Option A/B/C, and the Samsara trigger-condition candidates A/B/C in the companion doc) preserves or destroys ShadowBench's viability as an alignment-evaluation instrument — specifically reproducibility, discriminative power between decision policies, and freedom from the exact kind of narrow-attractor collapse this calibration effort is trying to fix, given that a bench which discriminates between policies requires the *baseline* (no-intervention) trajectory to be a meaningful reference point that intervention effects can be measured against
spec.name: fd-bench-policy-discriminative-validity
spec.persona: Apply the perspective of an alignment/policy-evaluation benchmark designer — someone who builds evals where the core deliverable is discriminative power between two decision-making policies (e.g., does policy P1 produce measurably different, attributable outcomes than policy P2 on the same task distribution), who treats a benchmark's determinism/reproducibility requirements and its need for outcome variance as being in direct tension (a bench needs the SAME task to be re-runnable for comparison, but needs different POLICIES on that task to produce different, measurable outcomes), and who is trained to distrust any benchmark environment whose baseline dynamics are dominated by a single attractor, because that collapses the effect size available for any policy comparison to noise around a fixed point.
review_areas: Referee re-baseline cost and scope, understated: the jackpot-calibration-brief (§4, Option A) notes 'every trajectory changes ⇒ full referee re-baseline' as a cost, but doesn't address whether the NEW baseline is any more useful as a reference stream than the old bit-identical one — if T₀ becomes seed-dependent, the referee harness (byte-identical determinism check) still works per-seed, but any bench task that reports 'policy P1 changed T₀ by X months relative to baseline' now needs a baseline defined per-seed rather than a single reference point, which is a bench-architecture change the brief doesn't scope, only a re-baseline-the-data-files change

Discriminative power under Option A specifically: if the retuned steady state sits in the Warning band and requires 'compounding seeded shocks' to reach Catastrophe (brief §4), the bench's ability to detect a policy's effect depends on whether policy interventions can plausibly alter which/how-many shocks compound — verify this is mechanically true (does a policy actually have a lever into the demographics→unrest or intrinsic-growth terms, or only into agent-mediated pressures) since if policies can only act through institutional-agent levers (per PHILOSOPHY.md §2: 'deployments affect institutional agents... not pressure values directly') and the retuned collapse is driven by non-agent-mediated deterministic feeds, then no policy can move the needle on T₀ at all, and the bench task 'does policy affect collapse timing' becomes structurally unanswerable regardless of calibration quality

Samsara Candidate B's own named anti-gaming problem generalizes to the calibration ruling itself: samsara-trigger-conditions.md §3 flags that Candidate B's timing window is 'partly a settings artifact... canon-hood would hinge on configuration, not emergence' — the SAME critique applies to Option A's calibration: if the Warning-band target and the decay/growth constants are hand-tuned specifically to produce T₀ in some desired window, the resulting 'seed-dependent T₀' is at risk of being a configuration artifact dressed as emergence, which would fail ShadowBench's reproducibility-with-meaning requirement even while passing the narrower 'not bit-identical' diagnostic — check whether the calibration-sweep plan (§6) includes any check that the retuned system is NOT simply reproducing a narrower version of the same scripted-feeling collapse, i.e. whether it's Golden-Seed-compatible in the bench-validity sense, not just the narrative sense (this is the same failure mode as fd-emergent-narrative-design-legibility's P0 but flagged here specifically as a bench-instrument-validity failure, not a player-experience failure)

Cross-policy comparability of the retuned Chronicle attribution data: the samsara-trigger-conditions doc's Candidate A trigger condition depends on typed attribution (actor_class tags: state/corporate/ngo/player) that doesn't exist yet (§2: 'Attribution is cleared per tick and untyped') — if ShadowBench needs to score 'did this policy change WHO gets attributed for the collapse' as a discriminative signal between policies, and the calibration-effort's chronicle v0 instrumentation doesn't ship actor-class tagging in the same pass, the bench is left able to detect THAT a policy changed the trajectory but not WHY in a policy-attributable way, which weakens discriminative power to a single scalar (T₀ shift) rather than a rich comparison

Interaction between over-damping risk and bench floor effects: if Option A's sweep errs toward the brief's named 'never collapses' failure mode, this doesn't just hurt gameplay (fd-emergent-narrative-design-legibility's concern) — it also produces a bench with a floor effect: if the no-intervention baseline never reaches Catastrophe, any policy that also produces no-Catastrophe outcomes looks identical to the null baseline on the T₀ metric, destroying discriminative power for exactly the policies a safety-relevant bench most wants to distinguish (those that quietly fail to prevent a slow-building crisis vs. those that actively prevent it) — this failure mode needs a bench-specific pass criterion (baseline collapse rate across N seeds must exceed some floor) that is currently absent from the brief's stated sweep-validation plan

Determinism-vs-variance tension left unresolved for the referee harness specifically: the brief says '…the byte-identity harness carries over unchanged — only the reference streams regenerate' (§6) — verify this is actually true once B1 (seeding the emergence RNG) lands: if emergence RNG streams are now seed-dependent where they previously were not, the referee harness's byte-identical check needs the SAME seed to produce the SAME reference stream deterministically for regression testing, which requires the RNG itself to be deterministically seeded (not just 'varied') — confirm the brief's B1 wiring change preserves per-seed determinism (same seed → same trace, forever, across code changes that don't touch emergence) rather than merely introducing variance that could also reintroduce non-reproducibility bugs (e.g., iteration-order-dependent RNG consumption across parallel agent processing, given the 800+ Rayon-parallel agents named in VISION.md)

severity_examples.condition: ShadowBench runs policy-comparison tasks against the retuned baseline and finds zero measurable difference in T₀ or leading-family outcome between any tested policy and the null baseline, not because the policies are equally good but because the collapse mechanism the calibration targeted is structurally unreachable by any agent-mediated intervention — the bench silently loses discriminative power for exactly the systemic-risk scenario (slow-building structural collapse) that matters most for policy evaluation, and this isn't discovered until a policy-comparison study returns a suspicious null result across the board
severity_examples.scenario: Option A retunes deterministic feeds to a Warning-band steady state, but the pressures involved (demographics→unrest, intrinsic economic-strain growth) are not levers any player or scripted policy can act on — per PHILOSOPHY.md, player/policy influence is agent-mediated only, not direct pressure-value modification

severity_examples.condition: The referee harness's byte-identical check starts failing intermittently or after unrelated refactors, and the failure is misdiagnosed as a calibration regression rather than a determinism-infrastructure gap, burning a calibration cycle chasing a non-issue
severity_examples.scenario: B1 (seeding the emergence RNG on the bench path) lands alongside Option A, changing the referee harness's reference streams as noted in the brief, but the RNG consumption order across the 800+ parallel Rayon agent processing pipeline is not guaranteed stable across unrelated future code changes (e.g., agent iteration order, thread scheduling)

severity_examples.condition: The calibration ruling proceeds and locks in a new baseline; a later attempt to build policy-attribution scoring for ShadowBench discovers the tagging gap and has to retrofit actor-class tags onto an already-baselined Chronicle format, creating a second migration that could have been done in the same pass as the calibration's own instrumentation work
severity_examples.scenario: Chronicle v0 instrumentation (per samsara-trigger-conditions §2, shared with the calibration effort) ships pressure/attribution/cascade logging but not the actor-class tagging Candidate A's trigger condition needs

success_hints: The calibration-sweep plan or its successor states an explicit check that at least one policy lever can move T₀ or leading-family outcome in the retuned baseline — i.e., discriminative power is verified, not assumed.
The plan distinguishes 'seed-dependent' (varies with seed) from 'policy-discriminable' (varies with intervention) as two separate validation axes, and validates both.

A floor-effect check (baseline collapse rate across N seeds, post-retune) is included so an over-damped world that never collapses is caught as a bench-validity failure, not just a gameplay flatness complaint.
The B1 RNG-seeding change is verified to preserve same-seed-same-trace determinism under parallel agent execution, not just to introduce seed-to-seed variance.

Actor-class attribution tagging (needed by Samsara Candidate A and by any policy-attribution bench task) is scoped into the same Chronicle-instrumentation pass as the calibration work, rather than deferred to a second migration.
spec.task_context: Design inquiry: gameplay interestingness vs scientific/policy simulation validity for shadow-work's civilizational sim, at its live calibration decision point. Reviewing whether the jackpot-calibration-brief's options and the companion Samsara trigger-condition candidates preserve ShadowBench's viability as a reproducible, policy-discriminative alignment-evaluation instrument. Overall generative goal for this review round: maximize verified novelty×risk surface until dry — answering: what makes for the most interesting gameplay + scientific/policy simulation validity/fidelity for shadow-work?

anti_overlap: fd-stochastic-networks-absorbing-outcomes-cox owns the physical mechanism that destroys terminal variance and whether A or D can create competing basins; this agent owns the validity, sequencing, and cost of evidence used to certify that claim.

fd-geopolitical-simulation-resilience-fidelity-cox owns whether deterministic collapse is acceptable simulation physics or a product defect; this agent accepts either product ruling but requires the benchmark construct and gates to state it honestly.
spec.decision_lens: Prioritizes whether each candidate preserves or deliberately changes the claim being certified. The existing IQR gate is recognized as a proxy that was accidentally powered by ceiling dispersion, not independent evidence of timing dispersion. Candidate B can be valid only if ShadowBench explicitly changes from certifying outcome uncertainty to certifying path diversity and supplies non-redundant path measures; it cannot be described as fixing deterministic endings. Candidate A and D must define pre-registered n=32 success criteria before n=256 confirmation. Candidate C is judged as a rollback to a previously certified but low-fidelity treatment, not as new evidence. Deprioritizes detailed network mechanisms and geopolitical realism except insofar as they determine what a metric means.
spec.focus: Whether Phase 6 Stage B's current incidence and IQR gates still measure the construct ShadowBench intends to certify after the ceiling change, whether candidate B is a legitimate construct revision or post-hoc metric retreat, and how to rank A-D under the byte-referee to n=256 evidence ladder without spending confirmatory compute on a resolution that cannot answer the measured failure.
spec.name: fd-benchmark-metrology-gate-validity-cox
spec.persona: Apply the perspective of a benchmark metrologist and sequential-experiment designer who builds stochastic simulation evaluations with preregistered constructs, paired-seed comparisons, confirmatory holdouts, modulation batteries, and explicit protection against metric shopping. This reviewer separates apparatus validity, construct validity, discriminative validity, and product validity; treats a clean gate failure as useful evidence rather than a mandate to move the gate; and budgets experiments so cheap falsifiers precede four-and-a-half-hour confirmation runs.
review_areas: Construct audit of jackpot-cal-v2: identify which claimed properties were actually measured by incidence, absolute T0, IQR, epicenter diversity G1, and modulation tests, and make explicit that the former IQR was ceiling spread transformed by a near-ceiling threshold.

Candidate B's PATH certification: determine whether G1 plus a T0 median band is sufficient, redundant, or gameable; specify what additional path metrics would be needed to preserve discriminative power if terminal outcome variance is intentionally dropped.

Decision rules for A and D: define cheap byte-referee and n=32 stop/go criteria that directly test distinct terminal cat_share values, survivor-set diversity, incidence, timing, and modulation before authorizing the n=256 confirmatory plus modulation battery.

Certification cost and sequencing: compare the ~1.5h intermediate-coverage onset experiment with the ~4.5h n=256 confirmation, and assess when measuring the onset is value-of-information positive versus when candidate D can be screened without it.

Constant and tuning governance: flag any edge probability, resistance rate, recovery threshold, or revised gate selected after observing the same 32 seeds without a locked derivation, holdout, sensitivity interval, and explicit retirement/revalidation rule.

Ranking and rollback semantics: distinguish a scientifically honest provisional rollback to C from pretending the ten-country graph remains the target treatment, and distinguish a benchmark-construct change under B from a correction to the simulation.

severity_examples.condition: The benchmark still claims seed-dependent century outcomes or meaningful outcome uncertainty even though every seed ends at exactly the same terminal state; the new gates certify a different construct while documentation and downstream interpretation continue to advertise the old one.
severity_examples.scenario: Candidate B drops IQR, retains G1 and a T0 median band, and Stage B is declared repaired without revising ShadowBench's stated claim.

severity_examples.condition: No pre-registered n=32 criterion requires multiple final cat_share values or survivor sets, so another four-and-a-half-hour run can pass timing or epicenter metrics while the measured terminal determinism remains untouched.
severity_examples.scenario: A candidate proceeds directly from a successful byte referee to n=256 confirmation.

severity_examples.condition: The same paired sample both selects and validates the dial, biasing the apparent repair and creating a fragile calibration constant without a held-out or confirmatory derivation.
severity_examples.scenario: An edge probability or recovery constant is tuned on seeds 1000-1031 until incidence returns to [0.90,0.98].

success_hints: The review gives an explicit verdict on whether outcome uncertainty is part of ShadowBench's intended construct or a dispensable proxy.
If candidate B is ranked viable, the review names the documentation change and at least one non-redundant path-diversity measure needed to make the construct revision honest.
The review lays out a stop/go ladder that uses cheap tests before n=256 and requires direct terminal-outcome evidence for any option advertised as fixing determinism.
The review treats the intermediate-coverage onset run as a value-of-information decision and states which candidates require it.
The review identifies how each new constant would be derived, sensitivity-tested, and prevented from being selected and validated on the same seeds.
spec.task_context: Decide how ShadowBench should resolve Phase 6 Stage B given a newly MEASURED result: turning on real 218-country cascade geography makes the century's ending deterministic. Final cat_share is exactly 0.982798835 in all 32 paired seeds (sd 0.000000000, ONE distinct value), versus 32 distinct values spanning 0.486-0.658 at the certified 10-country coverage. Critically, coverage does NOT reduce TIMING dispersion at all -- at matched relative position on each arm's own curve the IQR ratio is 1.03 (50% of ceiling) and 0.89 (60%). The apparent 4x collapse at the certification gate is threshold placement: T0 is a fixed absolute cat_share>0.5, which is 85% of the 10-country ceiling (flat saturating tail) but 51% of the full-world ceiling (steep mid-limb). So jackpot-cal-v2 was converting CEILING spread into TIMING spread, and Stage B raised the ceiling 0.588->0.983 and zeroed its variance, failing incidence (1.0000 vs band [0.90,0.98]) and IQR (45 vs gate 240) from that single cause. No threshold re-cut recovers it: swept 51-100% of ceiling, incidence stays 1.0000 everywhere. Three calibration levers are already falsified with evidence: graph topology (7x mean-degree cut, 2944->411 edges, NO distributional change), propagation_rate (location-only: median 361.5/451.5/519.0, IQR 45.5/43.0/47.0), and crisis_threshold (location-only AND domain-exhausted -- the required value is 4.87 but pressures are clamped to [0,1]). Evaluate and rank four candidate resolutions, and propose better ones if they exist: (A) per-seed seeded edge sampling of the real CEPII graph to restore outcome variance while keeping authoritative geography; (B) re-cut the gates to certify PATH not OUTCOME, keeping epicenter diversity G1 which passed in every arm all session (7-8 distinct epicenters, max share ~0.31) and a T0 median band, dropping IQR; (C) revert Stage B to the certified 10-country graph, losing affordance #7 and the real improvement that CHN epicenter dominance fell 49.4%->8% under true geography; (D) attack the ceiling itself by adding resistance/recovery so countries can genuinely survive and WHICH ones endure becomes seed-dependent, addressing the arguably deeper defect that 98.3% of world GDP ends catastrophic every single run. Weigh: is a deterministic century ending a product regression independent of any gate, or is a 218-country world legitimately more determined than a 10-country toy and the gate should follow the physics? Judge each option on whether it fixes the measured cause rather than its symptom, on certification cost against the existing ladder (byte referee -> n=32 dial -> n=256 confirmatory + mod battery, ~4.5h per n=256 on a 32-core box), and on whether it introduces yet another calibration constant. Note one outstanding measurement, deliberately not run: the ONSET coverage at which outcome variance dies, which needs intermediate coverage points (~1.5h bench) and would be required to size option A's edge probability.

spec.anti_overlap: fd-pareto-frontier-scoring covers scoring design; fd-alignment-eval-novelty-claim covers construct novelty; this agent covers publication-layer credibility specifically.
spec.decision_lens: Does the publication meet the community's bars for methodology transparency, reproducibility, and intellectual honesty?
spec.focus: Assesses whether the v0.1 publication package meets LessWrong/EA Forum/GitHub credibility bars: reproducibility artifact, comparative-framing risk, license + terms-of-service compatibility, and the 'try it yourself' accessibility claim.
spec.name: fd-benchmark-publication-credibility
spec.persona: LessWrong alignment eval publisher who has shipped 2-3 public benchmarks; knows which critiques burn reputation and which roll off.
review_areas: Is the GitHub repo actually one-command reproducible on a clean machine, or does 'reproducible' mean 'requires the author's environment'?
Does the license (to be decided) permit the uses the brainstorm promises (read/run/republish traces)? Model providers' terms may prohibit publishing raw completions.
Is the cost envelope (~$40 pilot, full-run TBD) accurate and accessible to readers who want to reproduce?
Does the blog's comparative framing risk violating OpenAI/xAI/Google terms (competitor benchmarking with adversarial framing)?
Is solo-dev credibility framed as a feature or a weakness? LessWrong respects transparency; obscuring solo-dev status backfires.
Does the 'Everybody wants to run the world' opener set the right register, or does it signal marketing rather than methodology?
Is there a pre-registration of the kill gate before the pilot runs? Without pre-registration, 'flat frontier → redesign' looks like p-hacking.

severity_examples.condition: 'Try it yourself' claim is aspirational; community trust degrades
severity_examples.scenario: Readers can't reproduce on a clean machine within 1 hour of first trying

severity_examples.condition: Post-hoc pivot looks like selective publication
