Does not cover how politics functions as a tribal signal or identity-marker in cultural studies — that is fd-political-identity-tribal-signal.
Does not cover cross-cultural and non-Western political identity — that is fd-cross-cultural-politics-coverage.
spec.decision_lens: For each of the 8 proposed values as a 'current' politics-coding, what are the 2-3 most empirically common 'formative' values that produce it — and does the draft's value set support expressing those trajectories without remainder?
spec.focus: Generational and life-stage political trajectories: what voter research, ANES panel data, Pew political typology, and generational cohort analysis tell us about how politics shifts across a life — and whether the proposed formative × current pair design generates the actually-prevalent trajectories while avoiding over-coding rare ones as defaults
spec.name: fd-political-behavior-trajectory
spec.persona: Apply the perspective of a political behavior researcher with familiarity with ANES longitudinal panel data, Pew's political typology studies, and generational cohort analysis (Millennial, GenX, Boomer, Silent) — they care about which political trajectories are empirically common vs. rare, measure success by whether the 8-value draft can express the most prevalent life-stage trajectories (the young mobilized voter who becomes habituated-and-disengaged; the New Deal Democrat whose county flipped), and flag any trajectory that the draft encodes as a default but that empirical research shows is statistically rare.
review_areas: The ANES panel data finding most relevant to this axis: political identification is overwhelmingly stable across adulthood. Only about 10-15% of adults show genuine partisan conversion; the rest show stability or drift toward the mean. Assess whether the draft's probability distribution honors this finding: if 'disaffected' is at 12% and 'true-believer' at 10%, these should represent genuine conversion/commitment rates — but if 'traditionally-loyal' at 25% is the modal type, what are the most common formative values that produce 'traditionally-loyal' current, and are those formative values expressible in the same 8-value set?

Generational cohort analysis (Strauss and Howe's generational archetypes aside — use the more empirically grounded Pew typology): Silent Generation political formation was civic-organization-mediated and broadcast-era; Boomers split along the Vietnam/counterculture fault line; GenX is characterized by low civic engagement and high skepticism ('post-political' in the draft's terms); Millennials show high initial mobilization followed by rapid disillusionment post-2016; GenZ is forming in the platform-aggregator era. Assess whether the formative × current pair design, combined with the chronological-era axis, generates the generation-specific trajectories that a player would recognize — the GenX post-political Unc, the Boomer true-believer-turned-disaffected, the Millennial burnout.

Pew's 2021 Political Typology identified 9 types in the US public: Progressive Left, Establishment Liberals, Democratic Mainstays, Outsider Left, Stressed Sideliners, Ambivalent Right, Populist Right, Committed Conservatives, Faith and Flag Conservatives. Assess which of Pew's 9 types the 8-value draft can express and which it cannot. This is not a proposal to adopt Pew's labels (most are position-coded and violate the brief's dignity rule) but a coverage test: do the 8 posture values, combined with class × region × media-era, generate Pew's full typology through cross-products — or do some Pew types (Outsider Left, Stressed Sideliners) fall through the draft's value space?

The 'life-stage politics' research tradition (Holbrook, 'Do Campaigns Matter?'; Plutzer, 'Becoming a Habitual Voter'): early voting experience has a disproportionate effect on political formation — the Unc who first voted in 1972 (Nixon landslide), 1980 (Reagan), 1992 (Clinton-Perot), 2008 (Obama), or 2016 carries a formative event-imprint that shapes his current politics. Assess whether the chronological-era axis (already locked) is doing enough of this work, or whether the politics-formative value needs to be expressible in terms of political-era as well as posture (the 'true-believer' formed in 2008's optimism vs. the 'true-believer' formed in 1980's backlash-politics are very different Uncs).

The 'vocationally-absorbed' → 'single-issue-coded' trajectory in the draft (the career-ending-injury healthcare policy Unc): assess this against the ANES single-issue voter literature. Single-issue voting is empirically associated with specific issue-domains (abortion, gun rights, immigration, Israel/Palestine) and specific personal-history triggers (the bereaved parent, the veteran, the cancer survivor). Evaluate whether 'single-issue-coded' at 3% matches the empirical prevalence — and whether the draft's single-issue value can generate the full range of single-issue Uncs (not just politically convenient ones that read as sympathetic from the designer's vantage point, but also single-issue Uncs whose anchor issue the designer may find uncomfortable).

The disillusioned-Democrat / disaffected-Republican trajectories: ANES data shows distinct patterns for each direction. Former-Democrats who become Republican (rare; tends to be economics-driven, especially Rust Belt manufacturing) vs. former-Republicans who become independent (more common post-2012 among suburban college-educated professionals, post-2020 among anti-Trump conservatives). Assess whether 'disaffected' as a single value is grain-coherent enough to cover both directions — or whether the directionality of disaffection is characterologically load-bearing (the ex-Democrat Unc carries a different type-of-guy flavor than the ex-Republican Unc, even when both are currently 'disaffected').

severity_examples.condition: Pew's 'Stressed Sideliners' — politically disengaged, low information, not ideological, not loyal, overwhelmed — are one of the largest actual groups in the US public. If none of the 8 values generates this type (disaffected requires former engagement; post-political requires former energy; vocationally-absorbed requires a trade to structure around), the draft has a coverage gap in its modal population. A recognizable Unc type — the guy who genuinely does not track politics, is not making a philosophical statement, just doesn't — is absent.
severity_examples.scenario: Stressed Sideliners (Pew's largest group at ~15%) have no home in the 8-value draft

severity_examples.condition: If the formative × current pair design requires 'true-believer' (formative) → 'disaffected' (current) to generate both the ex-organizer Unc and the ex-talk-radio Unc, and the downstream characterization cannot distinguish them — the Unc's vocabulary, cultural references, and relationship to politics will be identical regardless of which side he came from — the value is underdetermined for trajectory-based characterization.
severity_examples.scenario: 'disaffected' collapses ex-Democrat and ex-Republican trajectories into an indistinct type

severity_examples.condition: If the chronological-era axis (locked at 8 values: mid-century → 2020s) is not wired into the politics-formative value's characterization output, then a true-believer formed by Obama-era optimism and a true-believer formed by Reagan-era backlash-politics will produce the same type-of-guy flavor. The brief specifies that media-era × class × region will bias the politics-coding — but without explicit formative-era × politics-value interaction, this disambiguation may not happen downstream.
severity_examples.scenario: The 2008-formative 'true-believer' and the 1980-formative 'true-believer' generate indistinguishable Uncs

success_hints: Run the Pew coverage test: list the 8 posture values and map each Pew typology segment to its closest draft value. If any segment has no close mapping, that is a coverage gap. Then check whether the gap matters for player recognition.

The ANES stability check: does the draft's trajectory design honor the empirical finding that most political identity is stable? A trajectory-pair design that implies conversion as a common occurrence overestimates how often Uncs change their politics — the formative × current pair should produce the same value most of the time, with divergent pairs as characterologically interesting exceptions, not defaults.

For single-issue-coded: generate 5 specific single-issue Uncs from different ends of the political spectrum. If all 5 feel sympathetic or all 5 feel credulous, the value is being applied selectively in the design — it should generate equally dignified characters anchored by gun-rights, abortion, environment, criminal-justice, and Israel/Palestine.
spec.task_context: Reviewing the 8-value politics-coding draft for Unc Rancher through a political behavior and voter-research lens — assessing whether the value set and formative × current trajectory design produce empirically common political trajectories, identifying population segments with no home in the draft, and checking that the probability distribution reflects actual political-identity prevalence rather than designer-salience weighting.

anti_overlap: Does not cover the structural question of axis count or grain-coherence taxonomy — that is fd-political-sociology-axis-structure.
Does not cover cross-cultural political identity outside the US — that is fd-cross-cultural-politics-coverage.
Does not cover game-design craft for avoiding mockery in procedural character systems — that is fd-procedural-politics-craft.
spec.decision_lens: For each of the 8 values: does the name and description encode the value as a social-identity and belonging-signal, or does it secretly encode it as a deficit of reasoning (not thinking for oneself, being tribal, being naive, being reactionary) — and does the dignity audit pass equally for values pointing toward political orientations the designer is likely to be sympathetic to vs. unsympathetic to?
spec.focus: Politics as identity-performance rather than position-holding: apply Mason's 'Uncivil Agreement,' Achen and Bartels' 'Democracy for Realists,' and Berlant's cruel optimism to evaluate whether each of the 8 draft values encodes politics as a substance (positions held) or a signal (identity transmitted) — and to apply the dignity rule most rigorously, since the risk of designer-contempt is highest when values secretly code 'positions I disagree with' as types
spec.name: fd-political-identity-tribal-signal
spec.persona: Apply the perspective of a cultural-studies scholar of political identity working in the tradition of Lilliana Mason ('Uncivil Agreement'), Achen and Bartels ('Democracy for Realists'), and Lauren Berlant (cruel optimism applied to political attachment) — they care about whether each politics value encodes politics as identity-performance and social-belonging rather than as rational position-selection, measure success by whether every value respects the dignity rule equally regardless of the political direction it points, and flag any value whose name or description contains covert contempt — including contempt that reads as neutral or empirical but actually encodes 'the kind of guy who doesn't think carefully' vs. 'the kind of guy who does.'
review_areas: Achen and Bartels' central thesis in 'Democracy for Realists': voters do not choose parties based on policy; they adopt the policy positions of the party they identify with for social-identity reasons. This means that a 'true-believer' Unc — someone who holds his side's frame as descriptive-of-reality — is not epistemically deficient; he is doing exactly what Achen and Bartels document as normal human political cognition. Assess whether 'true-believer' as named and described passes the dignity test or whether the name carries a subtle condescension toward genuine political commitment. Compare: 'true-believer' as applied to a DSA-organizer vs. applied to a talk-radio conservative — does the description feel equally dignified in both directions?

Mason's finding on 'identity-party sorting': in highly sorted political environments, expressing a political identity is primarily a statement of social belonging rather than ideological commitment. Apply this to 'traditionally-loyal': the brief's framing ('loyalty is the substrate, not the issues') is Mason-correct. But assess whether the description passes the dignity test for all versions of traditional loyalty — the boston-Irish Democrat grandfather example is sympathetic; would the description be equally dignified and non-condescending applied to a deep-South Republican family? The test is: can a player of any political background see this value applied to their own family and feel respected?

Berlant's cruel-optimism framework applied to 'disaffected': cruel optimism names an attachment to a good-life script that has stopped working but that the subject cannot relinquish. The brief correctly identifies 'disaffected' as Berlant-coded. But assess whether the description honors the Berlant framing — that the attachment is not a mistake or a failure of perception, but a structurally-produced condition — or whether 'disaffected' risks reading as 'the guy who gave up' or 'the guy who figured out the game is rigged' (both of which encode a value-judgment about his response). Berlant's point is that the object of attachment is genuinely gone, not that the subject is deficient for having been attached.

The 'oppositional' dignity problem is the highest-risk single value in the draft. The brief flags it explicitly: 'does this risk being a designer-side label for people I disagree with?' Assess this rigorously: 'oppositional' as described ('defined by what he's against, regardless of side; professional contrarian; IDW-coded; perpetual skeptic') gives a left-coded example (anti-tech Luddite) and a right-coded example (anti-woke), but the label itself — 'oppositional' — is structurally asymmetric. The Luddite is oppositional-to-power; the anti-woke is oppositional-to-culture. These are not the same posture toward politics. Assess whether 'oppositional' is a grain-coherent value or a basket for 'types who resist something I happen to respect, regardless of side.'

The 'single-issue-coded' dignity risk: the brief flags this specifically as risking 'flattening real metis-politics into a category-of-fanatic.' The bereaved parent gun-policy advocate and the post-traumatic veteran healthcare-policy advocate are given as dignity-restoring examples. But assess whether the 3% probability assignment is itself a dignity-compromising move: single-issue engagement is the most common form of genuine political participation among people who are not habitual partisan voters. Assigning it 3% encodes it as rare and therefore eccentric — which may carry implicit judgment. What does the Berlant framing say about single-issue attachment as a form of cruel optimism (the abortion-rights voter in a state that already banned it; the gun-rights voter in a city that banned assault weapons)?

The 'gradualist' dignity risk is subtle and easily missed: 'Both sides have a point. Wants modest, institutional, technocratic improvement. The Atlantic-subscriber Unc.' This description is written from within a specific class-coded political epistemology that treats moderate technocratic politics as 'having a point on both sides' — but Mason and Achen/Bartels show that this stance is itself a partisan identity-cluster (credentialed-class, institutionalist, media-ecosystem-specific) that presents itself as neutral. Assess whether 'gradualist' is coded with the same substrate-grounding as other values — or whether it is secretly the 'people who are like me' value that encodes reason and balance as its distinguishing feature, which is itself a dignity violation against non-gradualist types.

severity_examples.condition: If 'oppositional' is the value that absorbs IDW-coded, anti-woke, and perpetual-skeptic Uncs — and these are types the game's likely designer/player demographic tends to view with contempt — then the value name and description risk encoding designer-side political judgment as a type category. The §5 dignity rule is most likely to be silently violated here: the value appears neutral (it gives left- and right-coded examples) but the name 'oppositional' is evaluative (it encodes the subject as defined by resistance, which is a deficit framing). This is a P0 tone-risk if not resolved before the enum is locked.
severity_examples.scenario: 'oppositional' functions as a covert contempt-basket for political contrarians the designer disagrees with

severity_examples.condition: If 'gradualist' is described in ways that position it as 'the reasonable one' — both-sides, technocratic, institutional — while 'true-believer' is positioned as the epistemically-committed-but-possibly-naive and 'traditionally-loyal' as the unreflective one, the three-way structure encodes a dignity hierarchy that favors the designer's likely class-coding. Achen and Bartels show that 'both-sidesism' and technocratic centrism are as identity-driven as any other political posture — they are not more reasoned, they are differently socialized.
severity_examples.scenario: 'gradualist' encodes credentialed-moderate politics as the dignified-neutral default

severity_examples.condition: If the characterization output for 'true-believer' (vocabulary register, history-blurb tone, cultural references) is warmer and more textured when crossed with left-coded class × region × media-era combinations than with right-coded combinations, the dignity check has failed even if the value description is nominally symmetric. The test is not the label but the downstream characterization output.
severity_examples.scenario: 'true-believer' description implies the DSA-organizer and the talk-radio conservative are the same type with equal dignity — but the framing is more sympathetic to one

success_hints: The symmetry test: for each value, generate one left-coded and one right-coded instantiation (using class × region × media-era cross-products). Read both aloud. If one reads as a type-of-guy and the other reads as a commentary-on-a-type-of-guy, the dignity rule has been violated.

The Berlant reframe test for 'disaffected,' 'post-political,' and 'oppositional': does the description honor these stances as structurally-produced conditions (what Berlant calls cruel optimism — attachment to a form of life that has already stopped working) rather than as personal failures or choices? Framing as personal failure is the primary mechanism of dignity violation.

The Mason test for 'gradualist' specifically: can the description be read by a non-credentialed, non-institutionalist player as a neutral type description rather than as 'the thoughtful one'? If the answer is no, the value is doing covert dignity-hierarchy work.
spec.task_context: Reviewing the 8-value politics-coding draft for Unc Rancher through the combined lens of Mason/Achen-Bartels (politics-as-identity-signal not position-selection) and Berlant (political attachment as cruel optimism) — performing the dignity-rule audit exhaustively across all 8 values, with particular attention to asymmetric contempt risk (values that appear neutral but encode designer-side judgment), and assessing whether the description framing honors politics as a social-belonging and substrate-expression rather than a reasoning-quality indicator.

anti_overlap: Does not cover the mathematical composition of the CPT or multiplier semantics — that is fd-conditional-probability-table-design.
Does not cover the Zod schema or YAML pipeline implementation — that is fd-zod-yaml-schema-evolution.
Does not cover the roll-order DAG or deterministic-seed correctness — that is fd-procgen-roll-order-contract.
spec.decision_lens: For each of the 9 bias families, is the stated multiplier value derived from a specific findable empirical result — and if not, is the estimation method (e.g., linear interpolation from adjacent data, expert elicitation, design-team judgment) stated explicitly and separately from the cited-finding cells?
spec.focus: Political-science methodology fidelity for the 9 bias families: whether the YAML bias cells accurately encode the empirical findings from Ghitza-Gelman cohort imprinting, Inglehart materialist/post-materialist values shift, Achen-Bartels habitus literature, Jennings-Niemi panel data, Sears county-flip research, and Joe-Rogan cluster typology — with particular attention to the distinction between cited findings (source: specific-paper) and estimated values (source: estimate) and whether the estimation methodology is stated.
spec.name: fd-political-science-cohort-encoding
spec.persona: Apply the perspective of a political scientist with working knowledge of the Ghitza-Gelman MRP methodology, Inglehart's cultural values survey tradition, Achen-Bartels revisionist democratic theory, and Jennings-Niemi political socialization panel — they care about whether each numbered bias cell (multiplier value) is grounded in a specific findable empirical source or declared as an estimate with a stated derivation method, measure success by whether the `source:` field in each YAML entry is specific enough to be independently verified (author-year-finding, not just author), and flag any cell whose stated number is not supported by the cited finding or whose source citation is vague enough to be unfalsifiable.
review_areas: Ghitza-Gelman cohort imprinting encoding: the Ghitza-Gelman (2014) presidential approval model finds that political identity formed during the ages 14-24 has disproportionate weight on adult partisanship, with the effect peaking at approximately age 18 and decaying logarithmically thereafter. The brainstorm cites this as one of the 9 bias families but does not specify what multiplier values the finding warrants. Assess whether a correct encoding of Ghitza-Gelman would produce a `chronological-era × politics-posture` bias table where Uncs formed in high-approval presidential eras have elevated `traditionally-loyal` probability toward the president's party — and whether the specific multiplier values can be derived from Ghitza-Gelman's reported coefficients or require estimation.

Inglehart materialist/post-materialist shift: Inglehart's World Values Survey tradition finds a cohort-level shift in political values from materialist (economic security, order) to post-materialist (self-expression, quality of life) across generations in high-income countries, with the shift most pronounced for cohorts formed in postwar affluence (Silent Generation, early Boomers). The brainstorm cites Inglehart as one of the 9 bias families. Assess whether a correct encoding would bias `chronological-era=postwar` Uncs toward `gradualist` or `traditionally-loyal` (materialist security-oriented politics) and `chronological-era=platform-era` Uncs toward `feed-skeptical` or `dissenting` (post-materialist skepticism of institutions) — and whether these cross-axis biases are empirically warranted or estimated.

Achen-Bartels habitus recalibration: the brainstorm cites Achen-Bartels as the source for raising `traditionally-loyal` from 25% to 35-40%. Achen-Bartels ('Democracy for Realists', 2016) argues that most voters are habitual partisans whose issue positions are downstream of their party identity, not the reverse. Assess whether this finding supports a 35-40% marginal rate for `traditionally-loyal` (which requires additional data on what fraction of the electorate is habitual-partisan in the Achen-Bartels sense), or whether the 35-40% rate is an extrapolation that goes beyond the paper's findings and should be marked `source: estimate` rather than `source: achen-bartels-2016`.

Jennings-Niemi panel data encoding: Jennings-Niemi ('Generations and Politics', 1981) tracked parent-child political socialization across a 16-year panel, finding that parent-child political agreement is highest in the pre-college years and declines through the 20s before stabilizing. The brainstorm cites the 50%+ modal-trajectory (no-change) finding as Jennings-Niemi-sourced. Assess whether 50%+ is directly reported in Jennings-Niemi or extrapolated from their stability coefficients — and whether the '50%+' phrasing is precise enough for a YAML bias entry (should it be 50%, 55%, 60%?) or whether the flux-review pass (solwend-1ke-A) is needed to narrow the value before encoding.

Joe-Rogan / IDW cluster cell: the brainstorm cites a 'Joe-Rogan cluster cell' as one of the 9 bias families. This is the cross-product of `class=working-class OR service-precariat`, `region=platform-era-formation`, `chronological-era=millennial OR genz`, and `politics-posture=feed-skeptical`. Unlike the Ghitza-Gelman / Inglehart citations, this cell is presumably grounded in Pew political typology data or media-consumption surveys rather than political-science panel studies. Assess whether the source for this cell is specifiable at the precision required by the `source:` field — and whether a cell grounded in contemporary survey data rather than longitudinal panel data should carry a different confidence marker (e.g., `source: pew-2021-typology, confidence: medium` rather than `source: academic-finding`).

International regional cleavage distributions: the brainstorm explicitly identifies international regional cleavage distributions (UK realigned-northern-working-class, Continental Europe Christian-democratic / social-democratic / national-populist, Quebec sovereigntist / federalist, Ireland) as unspecified in the 2026-05-20 synthesis and deferred to the flux-review pass. Assess what the political-science literature can actually supply for these distributions: Inglehart's EVS / WVS data covers many of these regions and provides cross-axis political-culture distributions; Kriesi et al.'s 'Political Conflict in Western Europe' (2012) supplies class × political-posture distributions for the green-left / mainstream / national-populist tripartite split. Identify which sources are findable and sufficient, and which require `source: estimate` because no systematic survey data maps onto the Unc Rancher axis vocabulary.

severity_examples.condition: If the YAML entry for `traditionally-loyal` marginal rate carries `source: achen-bartels-2016` but Achen-Bartels (2016) reports party-identification stability coefficients, not absolute prevalence rates for habitual partisanship, then the 35-40% rate is an extrapolation. A reviewer who looks up the paper will find the stability finding but not the 35-40% number. The `source:` field should distinguish between `source: achen-bartels-2016 (stability finding, extrapolated to prevalence)` and `source: achen-bartels-2016 (directly reported)` — or the cell should be marked `source: estimate, method: extrapolated-from-achen-bartels-2016`.
severity_examples.scenario: A bias cell marked `source: achen-bartels-2016` encodes a value not reported in that paper, making the citation unfalsifiable

severity_examples.condition: If the Joe-Rogan / IDW / feed-skeptical cluster cell specifies a multiplier of 2.5 for `feed-skeptical` given `working-class × platform-era × millennial` but the source is not findable (no Pew typology paper reports this exact cross-product), the cell is an estimate masquerading as an empirical finding. In the flux-review pass, reviewers will be unable to verify or challenge the value. Marking the cell `source: estimate, method: design-judgment` honestly exposes it as a value-judgment gap that the flux-review should close.
severity_examples.scenario: The Joe-Rogan cluster cell is encoded with a specific multiplier but no specifiable empirical source

severity_examples.condition: If the brainstorm specifies `modal-trajectory: 50%+` as Jennings-Niemi sourced but the YAML requires a specific number (e.g., `weight: 0.55` for the no-change trajectory), the YAML author must pick a value within the 50-80% range without further guidance. Different authors might pick 50%, 60%, or 70% — a difference large enough to affect the distribution materially. The `source:` field should cite the specific Jennings-Niemi table or figure that constrains the value, and the flux-review pass should narrow the range to a single number before the YAML is authored.
severity_examples.scenario: The '50%+ modal-trajectory' Jennings-Niemi citation is imprecise enough to admit any value from 50% to 80%

success_hints: For each of the 9 bias families, require the YAML preamble to state the source citation precisely enough to locate a specific table, figure, or reported coefficient in the referenced paper — not just author-year. A `source:` field that reads `inglehart-1977 table 3.2` is verifiable; one that reads `inglehart-materialist` is not.

Distinguish three source tiers in the schema: `empirical` (directly reported in the cited source), `extrapolated` (derived from a reported finding via a stated method), and `estimated` (design-team judgment with no empirical anchor). Require that `extrapolated` entries also carry a `method:` field. Reject `empirical` sources that cannot be verified to report the cited value.

For the international regional cleavage distributions, run a pre-matrix research pass against Kriesi et al. (2012), Inglehart EVS Wave 5-7, and Norris-Inglehart (2019) before authoring the YAML. These sources cover the UK, France, Germany, Ireland, and Quebec; the research pass should produce specific numbers or honest `estimated` markers before the bias entries are written.

anti_overlap: Does not cover behavioral political science or voter research (ANES panel data, generational cohort analysis) — that is fd-political-behavior-trajectory.
Does not cover political identity as tribal signal or the identity-vs-position distinction in cultural studies — that is fd-political-identity-tribal-signal.
Does not cover game-design craft for politics-coding without mockery — that is fd-procedural-politics-craft.
spec.decision_lens: Which structural option (α/β/γ/δ) best models the sociological finding that political identity is a cluster of social identities rather than a set of issue positions — and what does each option require the downstream procedural engine to know about politics that real people don't consciously know about themselves?
spec.focus: Whether politics-coding should be one field or two (or three): apply political sociology's empirical account of how political identity actually clusters in real populations — Putnam on social capital, Skocpol on civic organizations, Mason's 'Uncivil Agreement' on identity-party sorting — to evaluate Options α through δ and determine which structural choice best models real political identity formation without encoding a position-map the engine must maintain
spec.name: fd-political-sociology-axis-structure
spec.persona: Apply the perspective of a political sociologist steeped in Putnam, Skocpol, Lilliana Mason, and the ANES panel-data tradition — they care about whether the axis structure reflects how political identity actually forms (as a cluster of social identities, not a chosen position), measure success by whether the structural choice produces character types that map onto recognizable sociological phenomena (the culturally-conservative economic-progressive; the economically-precarious habitual-Democrat; the post-Tea-Party disaffiliated), and flag any structure that requires the engine to maintain a coherent left/right position-map that political sociology shows is not how real people carry politics.
review_areas: Lilliana Mason's core finding in 'Uncivil Agreement' (2018): Americans have become politically sorted such that party, ideology, race, religion, and geography now align rather than cross-cut — producing high 'social identity consistency' rather than 'issue consistency.' Evaluate Option α (posture-only) against this finding: if social identity consistency is the dominant empirical phenomenon, does a posture-only axis (true-believer / disaffected / gradualist / etc.) capture enough of the sociological signal, or does it systematically miss the identity-cluster structure that Mason documents? A true-believer DSA-organizer and a true-believer talk-radio conservative share a posture but belong to entirely different social identity clusters — does Option α produce characters whose politics is legible without naming the cluster?

Putnam's bowling-alone thesis and Skocpol's research on civic engagement collapse: political identity in the post-civic-organization era is no longer formed through union halls, lodge halls, and civic associations but through mediated networks. Assess whether this generational change in political-identity formation is captured by the formative × current trajectory design: the Unc formed in the civic-organization era (UMWA hall, VFW post, Knights of Columbus) carries a different political substrate than the Unc formed in the platform era (Facebook group, podcast audience, Reddit thread). Does the politics axis need a formation-mechanism modifier, or is this adequately carried by the media-era axis already?

The ANES/Pew 'party identification' measurement debate: political scientists distinguish between 'strong partisan' (affective identity), 'weak partisan' (nominal affiliation), 'independent-leaner' (implicit partisan who denies it), and 'true independent' (rare; genuinely ambivalent). Assess the 8-value draft against this empirical distribution: 'true-believer' and 'traditionally-loyal' together may map onto 'strong + weak partisan' (≈70% of population), while 'disaffected' may map onto 'independent-leaner.' Does the draft's probability distribution (traditionally-loyal 25%, vocationally-absorbed 20%) match the sociological distribution — and if it departs from it, is that departure deliberate?

Option γ (posture + tribal-cluster, two axes) requires the engine to maintain a tribal-cluster vocabulary. Assess the sociological viability of this: political sociology has repeatedly found that tribal clusters are historically contingent (the Solid South flipped; the working-class-Democrat coalition broke), and that any tribal-cluster vocabulary will have a rapidly decaying shelf life. A game designed today with tribal-cluster values ('NPR-liberal,' 'talk-radio-conservative') will read as dated within 5-8 years as media ecosystems shift. Evaluate whether this is a reason to prefer Option α (posture-grain is more durable) or whether it is manageable (tribal-cluster values can be updated without structural change).

Skocpol's research on the Tea Party and its successors documents that political mobilization often happens through pre-existing civic and religious networks rather than through ideological conversion — the Tea Party was not a new political coalition but an activation of an existing organizational substrate. Assess whether 'traditionally-loyal' adequately captures this network-loyalty-activation pattern, or whether it conflates two different phenomena: (a) the Unc who is loyal because he never questioned his formation, and (b) the Unc who was activated by an organizational network and now holds strong positions he experiences as obvious common sense. These are sociologically distinct types.

The 'cross-pressured voter' in political sociology (Berelson, Lazarsfeld, Gaudet in 'The People's Choice') is the person whose social identities point in different directions — the union Catholic who is economically-Democratic but culturally-conservative. Assess whether the 8-value draft can produce cross-pressured Uncs: does a `vocationally-absorbed` Unc (IBEW: economically-union, culturally-conservative region) generate a recognizably cross-pressured character, or does the value flatten him into a single coherent stance? Cross-pressure is one of the most sociologically prevalent political conditions — if the draft cannot generate it, that is a coverage gap.

severity_examples.condition: If the review recommends Option γ and the tribal-cluster values are baked into the enum, the game's politics-coding will require active maintenance as the vocabulary of political tribes changes. A character described as 'NPR-liberal-coded' in 2026 may carry different connotations in 2031 as NPR's audience and reputation shift. The sociological finding that tribal coalitions are historically contingent means this is not a hypothetical risk but an expected maintenance burden.
severity_examples.scenario: Option γ requires maintaining a tribal-cluster vocabulary that becomes a political liability as media ecosystems shift

severity_examples.condition: If a posture-only axis produces characters whose politics is too abstract to recognize (the player sees 'vocationally-absorbed' and cannot infer anything specific about how this Unc relates to political events), the axis fails its recognition goal. The sociological finding that cross-pressure is common means the axis must be able to generate it — but if posture-grain is too abstract to carry tribal flavor, cross-pressure becomes invisible rather than characterologically interesting.
severity_examples.scenario: Option α (posture-only) cannot produce cross-pressured Uncs whose politics is legible to players

severity_examples.condition: If Skocpol's organizational-network-activation pattern and Putnam's inherited-civic-identity pattern both map onto 'traditionally-loyal,' the value is doing double sociological duty: the Unc who votes Democrat because his grandfather was a Democrat is sociologically different from the Unc who was activated by the Tea Party organizational network and now holds positions he experiences as always having been obvious. Both are 'loyal' in surface but have different identity-formation dynamics and different susceptibility to political realignment.
severity_examples.scenario: 'traditionally-loyal' conflates network-loyalty-activation with unreflective formation

success_hints: Test the structural choice against the Mason sorting finding: does the chosen structure produce characters whose politics is a cluster of social identities (identity-consistent) rather than a set of deliberate positions? Values or structures that require the character to 'have a position' on issues fail this test.

Apply the ANES distribution check: does the draft's probability distribution produce a realistic population of political types, or does it over-represent articulate/engaged politics (true-believer, oppositional) and under-represent the silent-majority types (traditionally-loyal, vocationally-absorbed) that empirical surveys consistently show are the norm?

Evaluate each structural option's shelf-life: which option requires the least vocabulary maintenance as political coalitions reorganize over the next decade? Posture-grain (α) should be more durable than tribal-cluster-grain (β) — but confirm this with concrete examples.
spec.task_context: Reviewing the proposed politics-coding axis for Unc Rancher's procedural character generator — specifically evaluating the Options α through δ structural question (one field vs. two vs. three) through the lens of empirical political sociology, assessing which structure best models how political identity actually forms in real populations without requiring the engine to maintain a position-map or tribal-cluster vocabulary that political sociology shows is historically contingent.

anti_overlap: Do not recommend making the taxonomy more statistically rigorous or survey-instrument-linked — flag grain-incoherence and dignity failures only when they would produce character-generation misses or dignity-rule violations
Do not address the game's ontology, walking mechanics, or lure design — focus solely on how polling-typology methodology reveals structural and naming issues in the politics-coding axis
Do not address the vocation axis or other locked axes — focus only on the 8-value politics draft and the structural α/β/γ/δ question
spec.decision_lens: The typologist asks two questions for each proposed politics value: (1) Would a political scientist cross-tabbing this value against class, region, and media-era find coherent internal variance — or would the cross-tabs reveal that the value is actually two or three distinct population clusters that predict different outcomes? (2) Would a respondent who belongs to this segment recognize themselves in the label without feeling categorized as a type the analyst finds risible? If either answer is no, the value needs to be split, renamed, or regraded to a modifier.
spec.distance_rationale: Orthogonal — professional political typology construction operates at the same abstraction level as the game's taxonomy problem (naming distinct attitudinal clusters in the political-affiliation space) but for a completely different purpose (predicting voting behavior and media consumption for research or commercial use). The polling industry has decades of hard-won practice in the exact problem the brief faces: encoding tribal political affiliation clusters without slipping into analyst contempt.
spec.expected_isomorphisms: Pew's self-recognition + dignity naming test directly maps to the brief's dignity rule — both disciplines discovered that segment names that encode the analyst's contempt produce taxonomies that fail their core purpose (prediction for polling, recognition-pleasure for the game). Pew's debate over separating engagement-level from ideological direction maps directly to the structural Option α vs γ question — the polling industry's resolution of that debate is empirically grounded evidence for the game's most important structural decision.
spec.focus: Professional political typology construction — how Pew, Gallup, Mosaic, and PRIZM segment voter/consumer populations into named clusters without encoding analyst contempt, what their cluster-validation methodology reveals about where the 8-value draft over-aggregates or mixes grains, and how the polling industry handles the dignity-vs-precision tradeoff when naming population segments
spec.name: fd-polling-typology-dignity-precision
spec.persona: Apply the perspective of a senior political typologist at a major survey research firm (Pew Research Center-level practice) who has spent careers building, validating, and defending audience-segment taxonomies to clients who span the full political spectrum. They care deeply about whether a segment name holds up under cross-tabulation, whether segment members would recognize themselves in the label, and whether the naming convention would cause a segment to feel mocked or condescended to if they read the methodology report. They have internalized the discipline's core finding: contempt for a segment leaks into the naming and invalidates the taxonomy.
review_areas: Grain-coherence of the 8-value draft against Pew typology practice: Pew's 2021 typology produced 9 segments by clustering on attitudes, not on positions — each segment is named for its affective-relational stance toward politics (Faith and Flag Conservatives, Stressed Sideliners, Outsider Left) rather than for its issue-positions or its tribal affiliation. Does the draft's 8-value list apply the same discipline? Flag any values that are secretly position-coded or affiliation-coded rather than posture-coded.

The structural question (Option α vs β vs γ vs δ) from the Pew-methodology lens: Pew's typology uses a single multi-dimensional cluster, not separate posture + affiliation axes. But Pew's own methodology notes show the analysts debated separating engagement-level from affiliation-cluster before deciding the cross-product was more predictive as a single cluster. What does the polling industry's resolution of this debate suggest about Option α vs γ for the game's purposes?

Dignity-preservation in the naming of `oppositional` and `true-believer`: polling typologies have learned to name segments for what they are rather than what the analyst thinks of them. `Stressed Sideliners` is a more defensible name than `low-information voters` — both point at the same population but one encodes analyst contempt. Apply this test exhaustively to `oppositional` (does it risk naming types the designer finds annoying?) and `true-believer` (does it risk reading as condescension toward genuine political engagement?).

Trajectory richness: Pew's panel tracking data shows that the most politically significant movement is not from one typology segment to another but from engagement to disengagement and back. Their longitudinal work shows `disengaged` as a major typology cluster that the draft's `post-political` only partially captures. What does Pew's handling of political-engagement trajectory suggest about whether `disaffected` and `post-political` are doing different work, or whether they should collapse into one value with a modifier?

Coverage gaps from the polling-industry lens: Pew's 9-segment typology covers populations the 8-value draft misses — specifically, the `Faith and Flag` and `Committed Conservative` clusters, which are not `true-believer` in posture but `traditionally-loyal` in heritage plus `vocationally-absorbed` in their faith-community political coding. Is there a genuinely distinct posture the draft cannot express?

Cross-cultural typology coverage: polling firms that operate internationally (Ipsos, Gallup) maintain separate typologies per country and explicitly flag when US-derived segment names cannot translate. For the game's international-region Uncs (British, Irish, Quebec, continental European), does Option α posture-grain travel better than Option β tribal-cluster grain? This has direct implications for the structural-question recommendation.

severity_examples.condition: If `oppositional` is the label the game applies to the IDW-coded Unc, the talk-radio skeptic Unc, AND the anti-tech Luddite Unc — all of whom see themselves as principled truth-tellers, not contrarians — the value is doing analyst-contempt work disguised as taxonomy. Polling practice would rename this segment to honor what it values (scrutiny, independence, distrust-of-institutions) rather than how it looks from outside.
severity_examples.scenario: `oppositional` is the most dignity-compromised value name in the draft: polling typologies have learned that naming a segment for what the analyst opposes (rather than what the segment itself values) produces a value that cannot survive cross-tab validation — respondents from the named segment refuse to self-identify with it, and the segment shows internally incoherent behavior patterns across cross-tabs

severity_examples.condition: If the review recommends Option α (posture only), the downstream generator cannot distinguish the `true-believer` DSA Unc from the `true-believer` talk-radio Unc at all — they will produce indistinguishable vocabulary registers. Pew's experience suggests the affiliation dimension is load-bearing for exactly the downstream outputs the brief specifies.
severity_examples.scenario: The structural question (Option α vs γ) has a direct analog in Pew's methodology decision to use a single-cluster approach vs. separating engagement from affiliation: Pew's own post-publication analysis showed that separating engagement level from ideological affiliation produced more predictive models for media consumption and message reception — which is exactly what the game needs from politics-coding (downstream into vocabulary register and what news he cites)

severity_examples.condition: When `post-political` is crossed with `class = working-class` vs `class = professional`, the game needs to produce different character signatures — but the value as currently described conflates Sideliner exhaustion with principled withdrawal in a way that makes the cross-product ambiguous
severity_examples.scenario: Pew's Stressed Sideliners segment — politically disengaged but not ideologically post-political, present across the income distribution, often citing exhaustion with political fighting rather than principled withdrawal — is partially covered by `post-political` but the draft's description conflates two distinct Pew populations: those who lost energy (Sideliners) and those who shifted from engagement to principled withdrawal (closer to `disaffected`). The cross-tab behavior of these two populations is meaningfully different.

spec.source_domain: Political survey research, voter typology construction, Pew Research Center typology methodology, PRIZM and Mosaic consumer-political segmentation
success_hints: Pew's naming discipline: a good segment name passes the self-recognition test (a member of the segment can read it and say 'that's me') and the dignity test (a member of the segment does not feel mocked by it). Apply both tests to all 8 draft values, not just the flagged ones.

The polling industry's core insight about grain-mixing: when a segment fails cross-tab coherence, it usually means the segment name is doing double duty — encoding both affective-stance AND tribal-affiliation. Identify which draft values are doing this and whether they need to be split or whether a modifier resolves it.

Pew's longitudinal finding that engagement-level is orthogonal to ideological direction is the strongest polling-industry evidence for Option γ over Option α — use this as the anchor for the structural-question recommendation.

Polling firms' international adaptation practice (Ipsos Global Political Compass, etc.) consistently shows that posture-grain values travel across cultures better than tribal-cluster values — this is direct evidence for the cross-cultural coverage question in the brief.
spec.task_context: Reviewing a proposed 8-value politics-coding axis for Unc Rancher, a procedural-generation system for recognizable older-male character archetypes. The review covers a taxonomy design question: is the axis correctly structured (one field or two or three orthogonal fields), are the 8 draft values at the right grain, and do they pass the dignity rule. Severity reference: P0 blocks, P1 required, P2 quality, P3 polish.

Do NOT review density as apprenticeship-readiness (thangka handles that)
Stay on the wayfinding/anticipation axis: does the player develop a calibrated sense of when the encounter is coming, and is the open stretch valorized rather than filled
spec.decision_lens: Does the game preserve the dignity of the long open stretches between encounters, or does it fill the silence with wildcards that signal the designers don't trust the silence?
spec.distance_rationale: No mobile-game designer would consult Pacific Islander open-ocean wayfinding on encounter spawn rates. The domain is pre-industrial, non-Western, has life-or-death stakes (missing landfall meant death by thirst), and operates on a voyage-scale (weeks of open ocean) that has no surface resemblance to a 30-minute urban walk. The mapping appears absurd until the calibrated-anticipation-vs-surprise mechanism and the valorization-of-the-open-stretch mechanism are named.
spec.expected_isomorphisms: The structural mechanism: in etak wayfinding, the palu calibrates expected encounters (islands, reef-lines, bird-zones, swell-shifts) along a voyage using a moving reference frame; encounters are *expected*, not surprising, and the long open stretches between them are the medium of the voyage, not a problem. The transfer: encounter density should preserve player anticipation (lure tells you what's coming) and valorize the un-encountered walk-time rather than filling it. Argues hard for option A and against option B's wildcard. Names a v0-relevant mechanism the other tracks may miss: the *anticipation arc* across a single walk, where lure metadata could give the player an etak-like sense of how close the Unc is.
spec.focus: Calibrated encounter density across an open-ocean voyage where missing an encounter (an island) means death, and where the wayfinder's calibration system (etak, star-paths, swell-reading) is the only way encounters are predicted
spec.name: fd-polynesian-wayfinder-etak
spec.persona: Apply the perspective of a Carolinian or Polynesian palu (master wayfinder) trained in the etak system of moving-reference-point navigation — they care about the calibrated density of expected landmarks (islands, reef-lines, bird-zones, swell-shifts) across a multi-week open-ocean voyage, where the dignity of the open ocean is preserved precisely BECAUSE encounters are rare and predictable, and where adding a 'surprise' island would shatter the navigational frame
review_areas: The etak principle: encounters (islands) are *expected* and *calibrated*, not surprising; surprise is failure of the wayfinder, not a feature of the voyage
Whether the player should know roughly when an Unc is coming (option A's guarantee) or be surprised (option B's wildcard, option C's gated multi)
The open-ocean dignity: kilometers of walking without an encounter is the *point*, not a problem to solve with density
The reference-frame question: etak uses a moving reference (an unseen island 'moves' past) — what is Unc Rancher's reference frame across a walk, and does encounter density disrupt it?
Option B's wildcard as the antithesis of wayfinding: an unexpected island in the wrong place means you're lost, not lucky
The signal vs noise calibration: how many false-positive bird-zones can a wayfinder tolerate before the system loses calibration? what's the v0 analogue for false-positive encounter hints?

severity_examples.condition: If option B's wildcard or option C's distance-gated multiples produce encounters the player did not anticipate from their lure choice, the etak frame collapses — the player has no way to calibrate their walks and the 'dignity of the open stretch' becomes 'when's the next surprise'
severity_examples.scenario: Encounters surprise the player rather than being expected by lure-frame

severity_examples.condition: If the UI, achievement system, or progress feedback treats the walk-without-encounter as low-value, the game has discarded the open-ocean axis and become a casino with steps; the open stretches must be valorized, not endured
severity_examples.scenario: The kilometers between encounters are coded as dead time

severity_examples.condition: If a lure summons an Unc but the encounter triggers at a random GPS point on the walk, the wayfinder has no etak — there's no way to read 'we are 60% of the way to landfall' from the environment, and the calibration loop the player would otherwise develop never forms
severity_examples.scenario: No relationship between lure metadata and *when* the Unc appears on the walk

spec.source_domain: Carolinian and Polynesian wayfinding traditions, specifically the etak system of moving-reference-point navigation as practiced by the Weriyeng and Fanur schools on Satawal and as documented in the Hōkūleʻa revival voyages under Mau Piailug
success_hints: Argue for option A on dignity grounds, but with an etak-style anticipation arc: the player learns to feel the Unc approaching
Frame option C as 'too many islands too close together — you're in an archipelago, not on a voyage'
Frame option B's wildcard as 'losing your bearings' — argue against unless wildcards are coded as wayfinding-failure rather than reward

spec.decision_lens: Are the v0 defaults visible, overridable, and instrumented in a way that Phase 1.7's calibration work will be cheap rather than expensive? Does the smoke test exercise the parameter axes that matter for calibration (sun_coefficient sensitivity, pace_mps variation), or only the formula's correctness at a single point? Is the persona-pace deferral (StepsDaddy stroll_mode = pace_mps=1.1) a clean handoff to a downstream phase, or a hidden assumption that the architecture can grow into?
spec.distance_rationale: An oral-tradition navigation system that costs each tack and leg against star paths, swell patterns, and accumulated experience is several disciplines and modalities removed from Python parameter defaults and smoke-test design, yet shares the deep structure of calibrating a per-segment cost against ground-truth observations one accumulates over time.
spec.expected_isomorphisms: A Polynesian wayfinder costs a leg as length-along-star-path plus a tack-penalty against the wind, with a default pace inherited from training (la'au — known canoe-speeds against known swell states) and refined through every voyage that survives. The pace number is not a parameter to argue about in the abstract — it is a calibration against the ground-truth of arrivals. Mapped: `pace_mps=1.4` is the wayfinder's la'au — a defensible default inherited from a tradition (here, public-health walking-speed literature), to be refined when Phase 1.7 has ground-truth (real OD pairs and route comparisons). The framework asks whether the calibration plan is structurally clean (parameter visible, replace()-able, smoke-test-instrumented), whether the smoke test is the right calibration instrument, and whether the persona-aware pace deferral is a clean handoff or a hidden assumption.
spec.focus: Whether the v0 parameter defaults (pace_mps=1.4, sun_coefficient=0.5, nan_fallback_value=0.5), the calibration plan deferred to Phase 1.7, the smoke-test design (test_smoke_apply_to_dtla and its wall-clock < 2 s budget), and the persona-pace deferral are structurally sound — does the v0 ship with parameters visible to tuning, instrumented against ground-truth, and honestly disclosed as defaults-pending-calibration?
spec.name: fd-polynesian-wayfinding-calibration
spec.persona: Apply the perspective of a Polynesian wayfinder for whom every pace estimate is an inheritance from training that survives only as long as the voyage arrives where it intended — for whom the default is sacred only until ground-truth says otherwise. The framework treats v0 parameter defaults as la'au-style inheritances, the smoke test as a navigation log, and the deferral to Phase 1.7 calibration as a planned port-of-call where the route is checked against arrival.
review_areas: pace_mps=1.4 provenance: SOLWEND_HANDOFF.md §7 is cited; the public-health literature on adult walking speed ranges from 1.2 to 1.5 m/s depending on age, gender, gradient, and observation methodology. Is 1.4 'typical adult' or 'typical young adult on flat sidewalk'? DTLA pedestrians span a wide demographic; the default should disclose its population assumption, not just cite a section

sun_coefficient=0.5 calibration path: brainstorm acknowledges Phase 1.5 synthesis finding 65 — 'may not discriminate in DTLA regular grid, needs empirical calibration in Phase 1.6 against actual DTLA OD distribution.' Phase 1.6 then defers calibration to Phase 1.7. This is a TWO-phase deferral chain; is the deferral chain instrumented (smoke test surfaces sensitivity, parameter exposed via replace(), TODO(phase-1.7) comment landed)? The brainstorm says yes to the comment; what about the sensitivity instrument?

Smoke-test parameter coverage: test_smoke_apply_to_dtla exercises one FeltMinutesV0() instance (defaults) against one graph (DTLA shaded). It asserts correctness, not sensitivity. A sensitivity asssertion (e.g., 'with sun_coefficient=0 vs 0.5, route ranking on a known OD pair shifts measurably or not') would surface the calibration question in v0's own test suite — at the cost of borrowing Phase 1.7's OD pairs. Is this borrow worth it for calibration affordance?

Wall-clock < 2 s budget on 12,880-edge graph: this is ~150 μs/edge for a function that does one dict lookup, one float cast, one conditional, one arithmetic expression. The budget is loose by ~2 orders of magnitude. A tighter budget (e.g., 200 ms) would surface accidental hot-loop regressions (a future weight adding a per-edge log lookup, a stray hasattr check). Is the loose budget defensible as 'this is a smoke test not a benchmark', or is it leaving observability on the table?

Persona-pace deferral cleanliness: 'StepsDaddy stroll_mode = FeltMinutesV0(pace_mps=1.1)' is the entire architecture for persona-aware pace. This is clean — but does Phase 1.7's A* know HOW to pick the right instance per query? The brainstorm says the persona-pace is 'designed for but out-of-scope', but the routing-engine handoff for 'which weight to use per query' is not named. review_areas: The brainstorm identifies sun_coefficient=0.5 as provisional (synthesis finding 65) and defers calibration to Phase 1.7, but provides no calibration affordance in the Phase 1.6 design. The frozen dataclass with replace() supports parameter tuning, but the brainstorm does not specify how to compare two FeltMinutesV0 instances' aggregate effect on the graph. The 'neutral' fallback policy applies a fixed 0.5 sun fraction for NaN edges. Portfolio risk parallel: treating unknown exposures as neutral (mean factor loading) is a common but analytically weak choice — it hides the sensitivity contribution of NaN edges from any parameter sweep. If 30% of DTLA edges are 'no_coverage', the effective sun_coefficient is attenuated by 30% regardless of what value is filed, which should be documented as a model caveat.

There is no mechanism to score two routes against each other using the same graph with two weight functions applied. Portfolio risk practice produces a 'tracking error' between model A and model B on the same underlying assets. The brainstorm should specify whether Phase 1.7 will expose a score_route(path, weight) utility so that calibration can compare sun_coefficient=0.5 vs 0.8 on a set of reference OD pairs.

The dataclass is frozen (immutable), which is correct for value semantics. But the calibration workflow implied by Phase 1.7 — 'tune sun_coefficient against real OD pairs' — requires generating many FeltMinutesV0 instances with different coefficients. spec.name: fd-procedural-politics-craft
spec.persona: Apply the perspective of a narrative systems designer with deep familiarity with the political-flavor systems in Disco Elysium (political vision quests, ideology as haunting), Crusader Kings III (trait-based political identity, dynastic loyalty as substrate), Citizen Sleeper (systemic precarity as political condition), and Pathologic (political authority as ontological ground, not ideological choice) — they care about whether the proposed value set produces politically-inflected characterization that feels emergent and substrate-grounded rather than prescribed and position-coded, measure success by whether each value generates a recognizable type-of-guy political flavor through downstream vocabulary and tone without requiring the character to hold or defend any explicit political position, and flag any value name or description that would produce mockable-from-outside characterization rather than legible-from-inside character flavor.
review_areas: Disco Elysium's political vision-quest system presents four political 'ideologies' (Communism, Fascism, Moralism, Ultraliberalism) not as positions but as hauntings — they are ambient presences, residues of historical formations that the detective-character encounters as worldviews-that-want-to-use-him. Crucially, ZA/UM treats all four with the same fascinated respect: each is presented as having genuine explanatory power and genuine failure modes, without the player being told which one is correct. Assess whether the 8-value draft can be written in this register — does each value have a 'genuine explanatory power' that the downstream writer can dramatize without needing to render the value as naive, cynical, or broken? Apply this test specifically to 'oppositional' (can the IDW-coded Unc be written with the same fascinated respect as the DSA-organizer Unc?) and to 'single-issue-coded' (can the gun-rights Unc be written with the same interior texture as the criminal-justice-reform Unc?).

Crusader Kings III's trait system: political identity in CK3 is expressed through trait bundles that determine behavior-under-stress rather than position-on-issues. A 'zealous' king does not argue theology; he acts in ways shaped by theological certainty, and players read his politics from the pattern of his actions. Assess whether the 8-value draft is designed for this downstream-consumption model: each value should bias vocabulary register, behavioral habits, and relationship-to-news in ways that produce legible political flavor without the Unc ever stating a position. Specifically: what is 'traditionally-loyal's behavioral-under-stress signature? What is 'vocationally-absorbed's relationship to political news (does he even have one, or does he only engage when his trade is affected)? What is 'oppositional's conversational habit (he challenges, he deflects, he points at contradictions — but never advocates)?

Citizen Sleeper's politics-as-systemic-precarity model: the game makes political flavor entirely diegetic — the character is politically shaped by the conditions he lives in, not by the positions he holds. His politics emerges from whether he has food, shelter, and labor-security, and from the social relations those conditions force. Assess whether 'vocationally-absorbed' and 'traditionally-loyal' honor this model — are they grounded in material conditions (the IBEW Unc's politics is downstream of his union's contract fight; the appalachian Unc's politics is downstream of what his county's economy does to his family) or do they abstract away from conditions into posture?

Pathologic's treatment of political authority: in Pathologic (both original and remake), political authority is not an ideology but an ontological condition — the Bachelor represents state-legible rational administration, the Haruspicus represents traditional craft-knowledge, the Changeling represents communal belonging. Each is politically flavored without holding political positions. Assess the 8-value draft against this model: does 'vocationally-absorbed' honor Scott's metis-as-political-form (§2.10) — the IBEW Unc's politics is the longshoreman's politics of jurisdiction and labor-rights, which is not ideological but practical-ontological? Does 'traditionally-loyal' honor hooks' belonging-as-ground (§2.4) — the Unc's politics is the shape of his community's survival strategies, which predates any ideology?

The grain-coherence check through a craft lens: the vocation review's key finding was that grain-incoherence within a value set causes tonal inconsistency in the downstream characterization — some values generate a character interior (caregiver generates presence and care) while others generate only a surface (commerce-large generates status without interior). Assess the 8 politics values for this tonal-consistency failure mode: does 'gradualist' generate a character interior (the specific way a technocratic Atlantic-reader relates to political events, his tone of weary reasonableness, his relationship to institutions he knows are flawed) that is as rich as the interior 'true-believer' generates (committed, totalized, reads everything through his frame)? Or is 'gradualist' a surface without an interior?

The original v0 sketch values that the draft discarded — 'hippie-residual,' 'Reagan-Democrat,' 'DSA-curious,' 'NPR-liberal,' 'log-cabin,' 'classical-liberal-edgelord,' 'apolitical-craftsman' — carry something the draft's abstract posture values may have lost: recognizability as culture-coded types. The game's central pleasure is recognition; the draft prioritizes dignity-compliance and substrate-grounding over immediate recognition. Assess whether any of the 7 original values names something real that the draft cannot express through cross-products — and if so, propose how to recover the recognition-hook while preserving the dignity rule. Specifically: 'NPR-liberal' names a very specific type of media-ecology-coded political identity that 'gradualist' may not fully capture; 'Reagan-Democrat' names a trajectory that 'true-believer → disaffected' may not adequately represent. From a craft standpoint, what does the draft gain and lose in the abstraction move from culture-coded to posture-coded?

spec.name: fd-procgen-roll-order-contract
spec.persona: Apply the perspective of a procedural generation engineer with deep experience in deterministic-seed systems for roguelikes and narrative engines (Caves of Qud, Dwarf Fortress, Wildermyth) — they care about whether the seed contract guarantees that the same `(walkId, lure.id)` pair always produces the same Unc regardless of which platform, engine version, or call-order variation is used, measure success by whether the roll-order DAG eliminates any lookahead (an axis's bias cannot depend on an axis not yet rolled), and flag any design choice that introduces non-determinism: floating-point normalization order, hash-function variability, or conditional bias application that depends on runtime state not derivable from the seed.
review_areas: Seed-to-roll-sequence derivation: the brainstorm specifies that `rollStubUnc({walkId, lure})` preserves the existing stub's deterministic seed via `(walkId, lure.id)`. The roll engine must derive a sequence of per-axis PRNGs from this seed such that (a) each axis's PRNG is independent of all other axes' PRNGs (no shared state that changes with roll order), and (b) the sequence of per-axis PRNGs is itself deterministic — same seed produces same sequence regardless of which axes happen to have non-trivial bias rules. If the engine uses a single shared PRNG and calls it once per candidate-weight draw, the sequence of calls must be identical across all code paths for any given seed. Assess whether the brainstorm's design addresses per-axis PRNG derivation or assumes the existing stub's approach (which may not be roll-order-stable).

Partial-order DAG vs. topological sort stability: a partial-order DAG over 8 axes admits multiple valid topological sorts. If the engine selects a topological sort at runtime (e.g., sorting by node name alphabetically as a tiebreaker), the sort must be identical across all runs and engine versions. If two axes have no ordering constraint between them, the engine must break ties deterministically — and that tiebreaker must be specified in the YAML preamble, not left as an implementation detail. Assess whether the brainstorm's 'defer roll-order contract to flux-review' position is compatible with shipping a deterministic engine: the DAG cannot be decided after the YAML schema is locked if the schema's `roll_order:` field is what specifies the DAG.

Lookahead prevention at the API boundary: `applyBiases(axesSoFar, candidates)` receives only axes already rolled. This is the correct API design for a partial-order DAG system. Assess whether the YAML bias rules' `when:` clauses can reference only axes that are guaranteed to precede the current axis in the DAG — and whether the Zod schema (or a separate validator) checks this at boot time. A `when:` clause referencing `politics_posture` in a bias rule for `class_current` would be a lookahead violation if `politics_posture` follows `class_current` in the DAG. This violation cannot be caught by Zod alone; it requires a graph-validation pass over the loaded matrix.

Floating-point normalization stability: the `applyBiases()` function normalizes weights by dividing each candidate's weight by the sum of all weights. JavaScript's IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic is deterministic within a single platform and engine version but can differ across platforms (x86 vs. ARM, V8 vs. Hermes) due to fused-multiply-add instruction availability and denormal handling. If the engine is eventually deployed to both a browser (V8) and a React Native app (Hermes/JSC), the same seed may produce different normalization results for the same weights. Assess whether the brainstorm's design specifies a fixed-precision normalization (e.g., rounding weights to 4 decimal places before normalization) or leaves this as a cross-platform risk.

Replay audit trail: the brainstorm specifies that the matrix is `source:` cited per bias entry, enabling traceability. Assess whether the engine's `applyBiases()` call returns or can return an audit log of which bias rules fired for each axis roll — the list of `when:` conditions matched, the pre-normalization weights, and the final sampled value. An audit log is not just a debugging aid; it enables the flux-review pass (solwend-1ke-A) to verify that the empirical bias numbers produce expected distributions over a sample of seeds. Without an audit interface, the only way to test the matrix is to run many rolls and check the output distribution — which cannot catch per-seed correctness.

Stub compatibility contract under seed: the brainstorm specifies that `lib/uncStub.ts`'s public interface is preserved and `solwend-1zp` replaces only the internals. This means the deterministic-seed contract must be preserved across the stub-to-matrix migration: the same `(walkId, lure.id)` pair must continue to produce the same Unc stable-id (even if the internals change) or the migration must be declared as a breaking change with a new stable-id namespace. If the stub currently generates stable IDs from a hash of `(walkId, lure.id)` and the matrix-backed engine generates stable IDs from a hash of `(walkId, lure.id, matrixVersion)`, existing saved Uncs from the stub era will have mismatched IDs — a data-integrity issue.

severity_examples.condition: If the engine resolves ties in the topological sort using JavaScript's `Array.sort()` (which is not guaranteed stable across V8 versions prior to V8 7.0) or using object-key enumeration order (which is insertion-order-dependent in V8 but not guaranteed by the spec), the roll sequence may differ between Node 18 and Node 20, or between development and production builds. A seed that produces `vocation → class_current → politics_posture` in development may produce `class_current → vocation → politics_posture` in production, resulting in different Uncs for the same seed.
severity_examples.scenario: The partial-order DAG topological sort is not deterministic across engine versions, producing different Uncs for the same seed

severity_examples.condition: If the YAML contains `when: {politics_posture: 'traditionally-loyal'}` in a bias rule for `class_current` roll, and `politics_posture` follows `class_current` in the DAG (so `axesSoFar` does not contain it when `class_current` is rolled), the engine silently finds no match for the `when:` clause and applies no bias. The YAML is syntactically valid, Zod validates it, the engine runs without error, and the output distribution is wrong for every `traditionally-loyal` Unc. This is the most dangerous category of matrix authoring error: syntactically valid, schema-valid, semantically wrong.
severity_examples.scenario: A `when:` clause in a bias rule references an axis that has not yet been rolled, causing the engine to apply zero bias instead of the intended bias

severity_examples.condition: If `uncStub.ts` generates a stable Unc ID as `hash(walkId + lure.id)` and `solwend-1zp` generates it as `hash(walkId + lure.id + matrixVersion)`, any Unc generated before the migration that was saved to the porch ledger will have a different ID when regenerated by the new engine. The porch ledger's `Unc` references will be orphaned. This is a data-integrity failure if the migration does not include a stable-ID compatibility layer.
severity_examples.scenario: Stub-to-matrix migration breaks stable Unc IDs for previously generated Uncs

success_hints: Specify the DAG tiebreaker in the YAML preamble as a lexicographic sort on axis names. Write a boot-time test that loads the DAG, enumerates all valid topological sorts, and asserts that the engine always selects the lexicographically-first one. This test costs nothing and prevents non-determinism from creeping in via future Node upgrades.

Add a `lookahead_validator` pass to `biasMatrix.ts` that runs after Zod validation: for each bias rule, assert that every axis referenced in its `when:` clause appears before the target axis in the declared DAG. This check is O(n*m) over rules × DAG edges and runs only at boot time.

Define `applyBiases()` to return `{value: AxisValue; auditLog: BiasAuditEntry[]}` rather than just the rolled value. The `BiasAuditEntry` should record which rules fired, the pre-normalization weight assigned by each, and the final sampled value. The audit log enables determinism testing: hash the log and compare across seeds to verify stability.
spec.task_context: Reviewing the brainstorm document for the Unc Rancher bias-roll matrix — specifically the roll-order contract and deterministic-seed design — to identify correctness failures in partial-order DAG stability, lookahead prevention, floating-point normalization, and stub-to-matrix migration that would cause different Uncs to be generated for the same seed or cause existing porch ledger references to break.
